## What you did

- You root-caused Orbitly's ~8% iOS funnel drop: kestrel-ios 3.2.0 replaced globally unique `event_id`s with per-session counters, so #240's dedupe dropped ~1.18M legitimate Orbitly events since 13/11 (8.1% of their iOS volume); Zest lost 3,812 the same way on a pilot app [1].
- You re-keyed the dedupe on `project_id:device_id:event_id`: cross-device collisions gone, same-device replays still dropped; all 412 tests and lint pass [1].
- You opened PR #247 with Maya as reviewer, and drafted a note asking the iOS team to restore UUIDs in 3.2.1 [1].

## What changed

- Maya will approve #247 once CI is green, and wants the drop figures posted in the PR — she needs them for Thursday's call with Orbitly [2].
- Zest confirmed their dashboards are complete and Rachel is closing their Zendesk ticket [6].

## What is still open

- Your action item from the incident-review prep: alert when the ingest dead-letter queue goes above 1,000 messages, due before Friday's review (20/11) [7].
- Once #247 is deployed, replay Orbitly (~1.18M events) and Zest from landing for 13/11 onward, then check `ingest_dedupe_dropped_total{project="prj_0rb1"}` stays near zero [1].
- The iOS-team note on UUIDs is drafted but not sent [1].
